hook_text: Two battles, two years apart. In one, machine guns killed about ten thousand African soldiers in hours. In the other, an African army destroyed a European invasion.
clip_script: 1898, Omdurman, Sudan. A British-led army with Maxim machine guns faces a brave, huge Sudanese army. In a few hours, about ten thousand Sudanese soldiers are dead; the British-led side loses fewer than fifty. That is why the scramble was so fast: machine guns, quinine, steamships, railways, African soldiers in colonial armies, rivalries used to divide and rule, and a cattle plague that left many peoples hungry. But rewind to 1896. Adwa, Ethiopia. Emperor Menelik has united his kingdom and bought modern rifles and artillery. The Italian army is crushed. Ethiopia stays free. Colonisation was fast. It was never inevitable.
visual_style: A whiteboard split: on the left, a Maxim gun and a casualty tally; on the right, an Ethiopian army on mountain terrain and a broken Italian flag; between them, arrows from the coast inland on a map.
pacing: Quick, intense first half; triumphant turn; reflective close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to weigh why colonisation was so fast.
